article_context: 介绍“高于平均水平效应”和自我美化研究，解释人们如何在记忆、照片与社交媒体中维持更积极的自我形象。语气是清晰的心理学科普。

article.title: 阅读 Text 2 · 我们为何往往觉得自己比实际更好看
article.background: 介绍“高于平均水平效应”和自我美化研究，解释人们如何在记忆、照片与社交媒体中维持更积极的自我形象。语气是清晰的心理学科普。

sentences.en: An article in Scientific American has pointed out that empirical research says that, actually, you think you're more beautiful than you are.
sentences.zh: 《科学美国人》的一篇文章指出，实证研究表明：事实上，你往往觉得自己比实际更漂亮。

segments.text: An article in Scientific American has pointed out that empirical research says that, actually, you think you're more beautiful than you are.

sentences.en: We have a deep-seated need to feel good about ourselves and we naturally employ a number of self-enhancing strategies to achieve this.
sentences.zh: 我们内心深处需要对自己感觉良好，因此会自然而然地采用多种自我美化策略来达到这一目的。

segments.text: We have a deep-seated need to feel good about ourselves and we naturally employ a number of self-enhancing strategies to achieve this.

sentences.en: Social psychologists have amassed oceans of research into what they call the "above average effect", or "illusory superiority", and shown that, for example, 70% of us rate ourselves as above average in leadership, 93% in driving and 85% at getting on well with others - all obviously statistical impossibilities.
sentences.zh: 社会心理学家已经积累了大量有关所谓“高于平均水平效应”或“虚幻优越感”的研究，并发现：例如，70%的人认为自己的领导力高于平均水平，93%的人认为自己的驾驶水平高于平均水平，85%的人认为自己与人相处的能力高于平均水平——从统计上看，这些显然都不可能同时成立。

segments.text: Social psychologists have amassed oceans of research into what they call the "above average effect", or "illusory superiority", and shown that, for example, 70% of us rate ourselves as above average in leadership, 93% in driving and 85% at getting on well with others - all obviously statistical impossibilities.

sentences.en: We rose-tint our memories and put ourselves into self-affirming situations.
sentences.zh: 我们会给自己的记忆染上一层玫瑰色，也会把自己置于能够肯定自我的情境中。

segments.text: We rose-tint our memories and put ourselves into self-affirming situations.

sentences.en: We become defensive when criticised, and apply negative stereotypes to others to boost our own esteem.
sentences.zh: 受到批评时，我们会转入防御状态，还会把负面的刻板印象套在别人身上，以抬高自己的自尊。

segments.text: We become defensive when criticised, and apply negative stereotypes to others to boost our own esteem.

sentences.en: We stalk around thinking we're hot stuff.
sentences.zh: 我们昂首走来走去，觉得自己相当了不起。

segments.text: We stalk around thinking we're hot stuff.

sentences.en: Psychologist and behavioural scientist Nicholas Epley oversaw a key study into self-enhancement and attractiveness.
sentences.zh: 心理学家兼行为科学家尼古拉斯·埃普利主持了一项关于自我美化与吸引力的重要研究。

segments.text: Psychologist and behavioural scientist Nicholas Epley oversaw a key study into self-enhancement and attractiveness.

sentences.en: Rather than have people simply rate their beauty compared with others, he asked them to identify an original photograph of themselves from a lineup including versions that had been altered to appear more and less attractive.
sentences.zh: 他没有让受试者简单评价自己相较他人的外貌，而是让他们从一组照片中找出自己的原始照片；这组照片里还混入了经过处理、显得更好看或更不好看的版本。

segments.text: Rather than have people simply rate their beauty compared with others, he asked them to identify an original photograph of themselves from a lineup including versions that had been altered to appear more and less attractive.

sentences.en: Visual recognition, reads the study, is "an automatic psychological process, occurring rapidly and intuitively with little or no apparent conscious deliberation".
sentences.zh: 研究写道，视觉识别是“一种自动的心理过程，会迅速而直觉地发生，几乎不需要或完全不需要明显的有意识深思”。

segments.text: Visual recognition, reads the study, is "an automatic psychological process, occurring rapidly and intuitively with little or no apparent conscious deliberation".

sentences.en: If the subjects quickly chose a falsely flattering image - which most did - they genuinely believed it was really how they looked.
sentences.zh: 如果受试者很快选中了那张经过美化、却并不真实的照片——而大多数人确实如此——那说明他们真心相信自己就是那个样子。

segments.text: If the subjects quickly chose a falsely flattering image - which most did - they genuinely believed it was really how they looked.

sentences.en: Epley found no significant gender difference in responses.
sentences.zh: 埃普利发现，男女受试者的反应并没有显著差异。

segments.text: Epley found no significant gender difference in responses.

sentences.en: Nor was there any evidence that those who self-enhanced the most (that is, the participants who thought the most positively doctored pictures were real) were doing so to make up for profound insecurities.
sentences.zh: 也没有证据表明，那些自我美化程度最高的人——也就是把美化得最明显的照片当成真实照片的人——这样做是为了弥补深层的不安全感。

segments.text: Nor was there any evidence that those who self-enhanced the most (that is, the participants who thought the most positively doctored pictures were real) were doing so to make up for profound insecurities.

sentences.en: In fact, those who thought that the images higher up the attractiveness scale were real directly corresponded with those who showed other markers for having higher self-esteem.
sentences.zh: 事实上，越是把吸引力评分更高的照片当作真实照片的人，越会同时表现出其他高自尊的指标。

segments.text: In fact, those who thought that the images higher up the attractiveness scale were real directly corresponded with those who showed other markers for having higher self-esteem.

sentences.en: "I don't think the findings that we have are any evidence of personal delusion," says Epley.
sentences.zh: 埃普利说：“我不认为我们的研究结果能证明个人存在妄想。”

segments.text: "I don't think the findings that we have are any evidence of personal delusion," says Epley.

sentences.en: "It's a reflection simply of people generally thinking well of themselves."
sentences.zh: “它只不过反映了人们通常对自己评价不错。”

segments.text: "It's a reflection simply of people generally thinking well of themselves."

sentences.en: If you are depressed, you won't be self-enhancing.
sentences.zh: 如果你处于抑郁状态，就不会进行这种自我美化。

segments.text: If you are depressed, you won't be self-enhancing.

sentences.en: Knowing the results of Epley's study, it makes sense that many people hate photographs of themselves viscerally - on one level, they don't even recognise the person in the picture as themselves.
sentences.zh: 了解埃普利的研究结果后，就不难理解为什么很多人会本能地讨厌自己的照片：在某种层面上，他们甚至认不出照片里的人就是自己。

segments.text: Knowing the results of Epley's study, it makes sense that many people hate photographs of themselves viscerally - on one level, they don't even recognise the person in the picture as themselves.

sentences.en: Facebook, therefore, is a self-enhancer's paradise, where people can share only the most flattering photos, the cream of their wit, style, beauty, intellect and lifestyles.
sentences.zh: 因此，Facebook 堪称自我美化者的天堂：人们可以只展示最上镜的照片，以及自己机智、品位、美貌、才智和生活方式中最光鲜的一面。

segments.text: Facebook, therefore, is a self-enhancer's paradise, where people can share only the most flattering photos, the cream of their wit, style, beauty, intellect and lifestyles.

sentences.en: It's not that people's profiles are dishonest, says Catalina Toma of Wisconsin-Madison University, "but they portray an idealised version of themselves."
sentences.zh: 威斯康星大学麦迪逊分校的卡塔利娜·托马说，人们的个人主页并非不诚实，“只是呈现了一个理想化的自己”。

segments.text: It's not that people's profiles are dishonest, says Catalina Toma of Wisconsin-Madison University, "but they portray an idealised version of themselves."
